slot.brief: Match haloalkane substrates with correct elimination/substitution product or reagent behaviour (e.g. Saytzeff vs Hofmann product).

stem:
Match each reaction in Column-I with its major product in Column-II.

| | Column-I | | Column-II |
|---|---|---|---|
| (A) | $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{Br})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{NaOC}_2\text{H}_5 \xrightarrow[\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}]{\Delta}$ | (p) | 3-Methylbut-1-ene |
| (B) | $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr} + \text{KOH(aq)}$ | (q) | But-2-ene |
| (C) | $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{(CH}_3)_3\text{COK} \xrightarrow{\Delta}$ | (r) | Propene |
| (D) | $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{Br})\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_3 + \text{(CH}_3)_3\text{COK} \xrightarrow{\Delta}$ | (s) | 2-Methylpropan-2-ol |

Choose the correct matching:

verdicts.working: A: NaOEt/heat gives Zaitsev but-2-ene (q). B: aqueous KOH gives tert-butanol (s). C: bulky base/heat gives propene (r). D: bulky base favors the less substituted 3-methylbut-1-ene (p).

working:
A: 2-bromobutane + ethoxide, $[?]$ E2; Saytzeff product = but-2-ene (q).
B: tertiary bromide + aqueous KOH gives 2-methylpropan-2-ol (s).
C: 1-bromopropane has one $[?]$-carbon; elimination gives propene (r).
D: bulky base abstracts a proton from the less substituted $[?]$-carbon; product = 3-methylbut-1-ene (p).

Independent check: A: NaOEt/heat gives Zaitsev but-2-ene (q). B: aqueous KOH gives tert-butanol (s). C: bulky base/heat gives propene (r). D: bulky base favors the less substituted 3-methylbut-1-ene (p).
